The bug was caused by the in-place mutation of the `security_scopes` list in `fastapi/dependencies/utils.get_dependant`. Because Python lists are passed by reference, when `security_scopes.extend()` was called, it affected all other dependencies sharing the same list object, leading to security scopes leaking across sibling dependency branches.

I fixed this by ensuring a shallow copy of the `security_scopes` list is created before any extensions are made:


This isolates the scope list for each dependency branch, ensuring that scopes added in one branch do not leak into others. I verified the fix with a reproduction script that confirmed that sibling dependencies now maintain their own distinct security scopes.
